winners.premise: A groom tells his family the bride cleans at the company she owns and introduces her assistant as her boss at their wedding.
winners.conflict: A bride must challenge her new husband's lie about her work without letting the correction become contempt for the cleaning work he used as a disguise.
winners.twist: The groom's concern is not privacy or the dignity of work but his wish to remain the main provider in his family's eyes.
winners.hook: My groom told his family I was a cleaner at the company I owned. Then he introduced my assistant as my boss.
winners.narration: His mother thanked Liv for giving me a job. Liv looked at me, then put down the champagne she'd barely touched. Tom tried to steer his mother toward the photographer, but I asked why she thought Liv employed me. He whispered that his parents didn't need every detail on our wedding day. I said owning the company wasn't a detail. I'd cleaned our first office myself, and there was nothing shameful about that work. The lie was the problem. His mother asked whether I was saying the business was mine. I said yes. Tom told her I was exaggerating because Liv handled so much of the daily work. Liv said she managed my diary and had never agreed to pretend she managed me. That was when he admitted he'd asked her to play along for the afternoon. He said his dad expected him to be the main provider, and I could have given him one day without making him feel small. I asked whether I was supposed to be smaller for all the days after it. He said we should discuss this privately. We would. We were already married, and I wasn't pretending one correction had settled what he'd done. But I asked Liv to come back to our table. She picked up her champagne and sat with the other guests. Being my pretend boss wasn't the job I'd invited her to do.
winners.title: The Boss He Introduced at Their Wedding
winners.description: His family thinks the bride works for the woman sitting beside her. Her groom has left out who actually owns the company.
winners.payoff: Being my pretend boss wasn't the job I'd invited her to do.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HER WORK DESERVES THE TRUTH

winners.premise: A woman discovers her sister has put her pregnancy scan on baby-shower invitations and falsely told friends she is carrying the sister's baby as a surrogate.
winners.conflict: An expectant mother must stop her sister claiming her baby while responding to the grief behind the lie without humiliating her.
winners.twist: The sister has mistaken a fantasy she found comforting for a promise someone else must now fulfill, and their mother wants to postpone the truth to save the shower.
winners.hook: My sister put my pregnancy scan on her baby-shower invitation. She'd told everyone I was her surrogate, but this was my baby.
winners.narration: Mum showed me the invitation and said I should be pleased Beth was finally feeling hopeful. I asked who had told her she could use my scan. Mum said she'd shared the picture, not expected a whole party. Then Beth came in carrying a yellow blanket she'd knitted. I asked whether she'd told her friends I was giving her my baby. She said she'd told them I was carrying it for her. I said those were the same lie. She started crying and said she couldn't bear another gathering where everyone asked when she'd have children. Mum asked whether we could just let the shower happen and explain afterward. I asked how many gifts people needed to buy before telling the truth became easier. Beth said I'd have a baby either way, while she was losing the only thing she'd been looking forward to. I told her I wasn't taking a child from her. There had never been an agreement. But I didn't want a room full of people laughing at her either. I said she could tell them herself, before they arrived, and I'd stay while she did it. Mum handed me the blanket. I put it beside Beth and stayed while she called the first guest. She said she'd lied about the baby being hers. The blanket stayed with her. I wasn't asking her to pretend to celebrate, either.
winners.title: The Yellow Blanket Beside Her Baby-Shower Invitations
winners.description: A pregnancy scan appears on the sister's baby-shower invitation. The expectant mother has never agreed to the story being told about her child.
winners.payoff: I wasn't asking her to pretend to celebrate, either.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HOPE STILL NEEDS HONESTY

winners.premise: A man learns his friend has invented an affair with him to explain savings she actually lost gambling, and wants him to confirm the lie to her husband.
winners.conflict: A friend must decide whether compassion for someone's shame can justify accepting a false affair accusation and helping conceal a financial betrayal.
winners.twist: The supposed romantic betrayal is a cover for another broken financial promise, and denying the affair will not by itself resolve the couple's real problem.
winners.hook: My friend admitted lying to her husband that we'd had an affair. She wanted me to take the blame for nine thousand dollars she'd lost gambling.
winners.narration: Neil turned up at my door asking whether I'd enjoyed the hotel rooms he'd apparently paid for. I told him there hadn't been any hotel rooms or any affair. He said Claire had named me herself. I called her while he waited outside. She asked whether I could just say it had happened once and was over. I asked why she would want him believing that. She'd gambled away nine thousand after promising him she'd never touch their savings again. If she admitted another loss, he wouldn't believe another promise. So she'd said she'd spent the money sneaking away with me. I asked whether she thought an affair would hurt him less. She said at least then they could talk about what had gone wrong between them. I told her she'd also given him someone else's door to turn up at. She said I was her closest friend and should understand how frightened she was. I did understand she was frightened. I still wasn't agreeing I'd slept with her or spent his money. I asked her to speak to him. She said I was choosing his side, then finally agreed to talk. I handed him my phone and stepped away. I didn't know whether their marriage would survive. But when he asked her where the nine thousand dollars had gone, she couldn't answer with my name.
winners.title: The Hotel Rooms That Had Never Been Booked
winners.description: Her husband thinks missing savings paid for an affair. The man she named discovers he is supposed to protect a completely different secret.
winners.payoff: she couldn't answer with my name.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF FRIENDSHIP CANNOT REQUIRE THIS LIE

winners.premise: A boss blames an employee for broken ribs after receiving CPR from him and tells him he no longer has a job.
winners.conflict: An employee must face losing his livelihood after helping in an emergency without accepting his boss's demand that he regret trying to help.
winners.twist: The boss's wife remembers the same event as someone answering her call for help, even though that gratitude cannot guarantee the employee's job.
winners.hook: My boss blamed me for his broken ribs after I gave him CPR. Then he told me I no longer had a job.
winners.narration: Gary called me into his office and pointed at his chest. He said I should have waited for somebody qualified. His wife had watched him collapse. She'd called emergency services and put the dispatcher on speaker while I tried to help. The ambulance crew took over. Now Gary said the pain afterward was damage I'd done to him. I asked whether he remembered what had happened before I started. He said he remembered waking up in hospital, which didn't give me permission to hurt him. Then he told me to leave my staff badge on the desk. His wife came in while I was collecting my things and asked why I was packing. He said he couldn't trust someone who'd injured him. She reminded him she'd been the one shouting for help. He told her she was being emotional because she hadn't seen what his recovery was like. She said she'd seen what it was like before the ambulance came. I didn't ask her to argue him into giving me another shift. I put the badge down and left. That evening, she brought a card signed by their daughter. It said thank you for helping Dad come home. I still needed another job, and a card wasn't going to pay my rent. But I put it beside my applications. I wasn't writing an apology for trying to help.
winners.title: The Staff Badge Beside His Broken-Rib Complaint
winners.description: He helps when his boss collapses. Afterward, the boss describes the same emergency as a reason to dismiss him.
winners.payoff: I wasn't writing an apology for trying to help.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HELP DID NOT DESERVE THIS
